To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new human hepatocellular-carcinoma cell line, DEL-SH-5, derived by in vitro propagation from a wedge biospy from the liver of a patient with HBsAg seropositive hepatocellular carcinoma, has been established and has been continuously maintained for 22 months.
a human hepatocarcinoma cell line has been established in vitro which releases HBsAg into the supernatant fluid.
a new cell line, DEL-5, derived originally from an HBsAg-positive patient with hepatocellular carcinoma, is a human hepatocarcinoma cell line which produces HBsAg.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) and its role in the development of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and the isolation and establishment of a new human hepatocellular cancer cell line which has the potential for continuous production of HBV.
the establishment of a cell line from a human liver tumour which has a capacity to produce HBsAg and is therefore a potential model for studying the hepatitis B virus--liver-cell interactions.
the establishment of a new hepatocellular cancer cell line, DELS-5, which is a human liver cancer cell line.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hepatoma cell line, DELS-5, has been established in culture and has the potential for HBsAg production.

DELSH-5 cells are a new human hepatocellular cell line, which have the ability to produce small amounts of hepatitis B surface antigen in vitro, and that they may be useful in further studies of the hepatitis-B-viruses--liver-cell association.
the DELSH-5 cell line has the potential to produce HBsAg in vitro and is a useful laboratory model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first report of the establishment of a human hepatoma cell line which is HBsAg-positive in vitro.
the DELSH-5 cell line is a human hepatocarcinoma cell line which is capable of synthesizing and secreting hepatitis-B-surface-antigen in small amounts.
the cell line is useful to study the interaction of the hepatitis-B-viral components with hepatocytes and the possible oncogenic potential of this virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DELSH-5 cell line has been established from a patient with HBsAg-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and that it produces HBsAg in vitro.
a human liver carcinoma cell line has been established which is capable of releasing HBsAg in small amounts into the medium.
the DELSH-5 cell line is a new human hepatocellular cancer cell line that produces HBsAg in the medium.
